subject: Score synchronization roadmap and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Score synchronization roadmap and next steps

Team —

Thanks again for joining the cross-team calibration sessions this week. We made good progress closing several discrepancies, but there remain three recurring sources of variance we need a concrete playbook for:

1) Anchoring differences — teams are using different level-setting examples for "Exceeds expectations" and "Far exceeds".
2) Midline compression — many managers default to the center and we lose signal between solid and high performers.
3) Dispute & escalation flows — reviewers disagree and there isn't a consistent triage path.

Attached I am sharing a draft checklist (score-synchronization-checklist.xlsx) and a short packet of anchor examples (anchor_examples.pdf). Proposed immediate plan:

- Monday (1/25): People Ops workshop to agree on 6 canonical anchors (individual contributor and manager tracks).
- Tues-Wed (1/26-1/27): Team-level recalibration meetings with local leads — use checklist, record decisions.
- Fri (1/29): Final review; any remaining disputes escalated to Laura + Hannah for resolution.

Action items for this thread:
- Marcus: confirm you can run the recalibration sessions for ML infra & runtime teams (target 1/26).
- Hannah: confirm availability to triage escalations on 1/29.
- Laura: confirm HR constraints/timelines for appeals and any required documentation.

Please reply with any blockers; I will consolidate sign-offs into the shared Drive doc and update the timeline.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: score-synchronization-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), anchor_examples.pdf (PDF)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Score synchronization roadmap and next steps

Thanks, Soojin.

I can run the recalibration for ML Infra & Runtime on 1/26, but two quick notes after skimming the anchors:

- The "Exceeds" example for senior engineers is skewed toward delivery impact; we need a separate anchor that captures technical leadership and long-term platform investments (that's what several managers actually reward).
- The checklist assumes a 60-minute team session — realistically for teams with 12+ ICs we need 90 minutes to walk through examples and loose cases.

I'll plan for a 90-minute slot and I can add two extra anchor cases focused on technical leadership. Attaching a small set of notes from my team (see calibration-session-notes.txt) — these are the recurring edge cases I want to surface.

-Marcus

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Jan 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Score synchronization roadmap and next steps

Appreciate the quick plan and the materials — good framing. A few HR constraints to call out before we lock dates: 

- Appeals window: we need to keep a 7-business-day window after final ratings are issued for documented appeals. That slightly shifts our deadline if ratings are finalized on 1/29 — appeals would need to be open through 2/08 (approx).
- Change logging: any rating changes post-calibration must include the manager rationale in the HR portal (link in related links).
- Confidentiality: anchor examples that mention specific employee outcomes must be anonymized. The anchor_examples.pdf you shared looks fine but please scrub names for the final packet.

I can run the 1/25 People Ops workshop and will bring a short template for documentation. Marcus — the 90-minute slot is fine.

I'll add a quick flow diagram and playbook to the Drive doc by EOD Monday. If we expect cross-org escalations (beyond the four teams), we should loop in Monica Patel from Global HR — tagging that as a conditional step.

-Laura

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 24 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Score synchronization roadmap and next steps

Thanks Laura & Marcus — really helpful.

Updates based on thread and the People Ops input:

- I've extended team recalibration slots to 90 minutes where headcount >10. Marcus, I'll mark your session as 90.
- Anchors: Marcus will add the two technical leadership examples; Laura will anonymize the packet and add the HR rationale template.
- Appeals timing: we will treat 1/29 as the tentative finalization date and keep the appeals window open through 2/08. I'll add that to the shared Drive doc and the checklist.
- Escalation: if a dispute is not resolved at team level, it goes to the People Ops review panel (Laura + Monica if cross-org). Hannah will lead the final technical assessment where necessary.

I've uploaded a new version of the checklist that includes: session length guidance, anonymization checklist, appeals logging template, and a short escalation decision tree. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/people/calibration/score-sync-2027

Please reply with a one-line sign-off by EOD Monday (1/25) if you can support the timeline. If I don't hear objections, I'll lock calendar invites and publish the updated packet.

Soojin

Attachments: score-synchronization-checklist.xlsx (v2)

Sign-off from me — happy to triage escalations on 1/29 and join Marcus for the ML infra session on 1/26 if helpful.

Two small asks:
- Can Marcus share his two technical leadership anchors by EOD Tuesday so People Ops can review anonymization?
- Laura: can you confirm Monica's availability if we need cross-org review?

Thanks everyone — I think this approach will reduce the midline compression issue and make the differences actionable.

Hannah
